userRequest: Choose a rate limiter for login and API request throttling in the existing Next.js application.
successConditions: The application limits login and API requests using stable keys already derived by repository code.
The limiter reports remaining quota and retry timing from every protected route.

identityFacts: Authenticated API requests contain stable tenant and route identifiers, and the login route derives normalized account and source keys.
dataFacts: The existing Upstash Redis database stores only operational counters.
operationalFacts: The edge runtime supports fetch but not long-lived TCP sockets, Node worker threads, or a durable in-process singleton.

hardConstraints.statement: Quota state must be shared across independently scaled edge isolates.
The candidate must use the edge fetch runtime without Express or Node-only worker facilities.

preferences.statement: Prefer the already provisioned HTTP-accessible Redis database.

reasonCodes.description: Quota state must be shared by every isolate.
The candidate directly supports HTTP-accessible Redis from edge handlers.
The candidate documents a fetch-based Next.js or Vercel Edge integration.
The candidate must satisfy the fetch-only Next.js Edge runtime constraint.
The supplied evidence does not establish compatibility with Next.js Edge restrictions.

unknowns.description: The accepted over-limit margin under multi-region replication has not been specified.
